items.title: A Small Model Asks Better: Fine-Tuning Query Clarification for RAG
items.summary: Researchers present ClariEdge, a dataset of roughly 3,900 examples for query clarification in retrieval-augmented generation systems. A lightweight fine-tuned LoRA achieves 96.6% classification accuracy and outperforms larger prompted baselines in recognizing ambiguous or ill-formed queries.
keyPoints: Introduces ClariEdge, a 3,900-example dataset for query clarification.
A lightweight fine-tuned LoRA achieves 96.6% classification accuracy.
The model performs well in both pre-retrieval and post-retrieval scenarios.

items.title: Scaling in Games: Continued Pre-Training For Embodied Agents
items.summary: A study investigates continued pre-training for embodied agents across virtual worlds by varying data volume, diversity, and model size. Results show that diversity aids transfer to related worlds, while scale improves data efficiency.
keyPoints: Investigates continued pre-training across 120 configurations and 4 model sizes.
Shows that data diversity improves transfer to related virtual worlds.
Highlights persistent performance gaps in distant worlds requiring richer training stages.

items.title: Agentic Harness Evolution via Successive Scale Racing
items.summary: Researchers propose Successive Scale Racing (SSR), a framework that optimizes agentic harnesses by adaptively searching for optimal evidence combinations and reducing validation executions.

items.title: Decision Language Models as Affordable LLM Judges in Clinical AI
items.summary: This study evaluates Jev, a decision language model that returns structured judgments, as a faster and more affordable alternative to large language model (LLM) judges for clinical artificial intelligence. Tested across pediatric answers, HealthBench criteria, and MedHELM tasks, Jev matched or exceeded many frontier and open-weight LLM judges while cutting costs by 73-294 times and execution time by 7-57 times.
keyPoints: Jev matched or exceeded the performance of 7 out of 12 LLM judges on pediatric answers.
Frontier judges cost 73-294 times more than Jev and took 7-57 times longer to run.
The model provides a scalable and efficient approach for clinical AI evaluation.

en.title: Decision Language Models as Affordable LLM Judges in Clinical AI

fr.title: Modèles de langage de décision comme juges cliniques abordables
fr.summary: Cette étude évalue Jev, un modèle de langage de décision fournissant des jugements structurés, comme alternative plus rapide et économique aux grands modèles de langage pour évaluer l'intelligence artificielle clinique. Testé sur divers cas, Jev égale ou dépasse de nombreux juges LLM tout en réduisant les coûts de 73 à 294 fois.
keyPoints: Jev égale ou surpasse la performance de 7 juges LLM sur 12 pour des réponses pédiatriques.
Les juges de pointe coûtent 73 à 294 fois plus cher que Jev et prennent 7 à 57 fois plus de temps.
Le modèle offre une approche évolutive et efficace pour l'évaluation clinique de l'IA.

items.title: Sketch2Sim: Framework for Hand-Drawn Circuit Analysis
items.summary: Sketch2Sim is an end-to-end framework that converts raw photographs of hand-drawn RLC electric circuits into executable SPICE-compatible netlists to compute nodal voltages and currents. Using YOLO detectors, a CRNN with CTC for text extraction, and image processing tools, the system offers a robust educational and professional tool across various handwriting styles and conditions.
keyPoints: Converts hand-drawn circuit diagrams into executable SPICE-compatible netlists automatically.
Employs a pipeline combining YOLO detectors, CRNN for OCR, and image processing.
Tested on a curated dataset of 1,000 hand-drawn RLC circuits to aid students and engineers.

keyPoints: Convertit automatiquement des schémas de circuits manuscrits en netlists compatibles SPICE.

items.title: Speedrunning Relational Foundation Model Pretraining
items.summary: The authors introduce modded-nanoRT, a leaderboard designed to decentralize relational foundation model pretraining using a single GPU. By fixing database calibration and applying typed trilinear attention alongside Muon and SIGReg, their recipe hits quality targets in 305.63 seconds on an NVIDIA H200, achieving an 8.11x speedup over reference implementations.
keyPoints: Introduces modded-nanoRT as the first speedrun leaderboard for Relational Transformers.
Achieves a training target in 305.63 seconds on a single NVIDIA H200 GPU.
Delivers an 8.11x speedup compared to the reference implementation.

keyPoints: Introduit modded-nanoRT comme premier classement de vitesse pour les transformateurs relationnels.
Atteint la cible d'entraînement en 305,63 secondes sur un seul GPU NVIDIA H200.

items.title: To Manipulate or Not: Opinion Dynamics in LLM Interactions
items.summary: This paper examines opinion dynamics in controlled LLM-to-LLM debates about climate-change attribution using models like GPT-6 Luna and Gemini 2.5 Flash Lite. The findings show that same-model interactions narrow opinion gaps while cross-model interactions widen them, and explicit instructions to persuade do not reliably increase conversational influence.
keyPoints: Introduces a controlled LLM-LLM debate framework to study persuasion and opinion dynamics.
Demonstrates that same-model interactions narrow opinion gaps, whereas cross-model interactions widen them.
Finds that explicit instructions to persuade do not consistently boost a model's influence.

en.title: To Manipulate or Not: Opinion Dynamics in LLM Interactions

fr.title: Manipuler ou non : dynamique des opinions dans les interactions de LLM
fr.summary: Cet article analyse la dynamique des opinions dans des débats contrôlés entre grands modèles de langage sur le climat. Les résultats montrent que les interactions entre modèles similaires réduisent l'écart d'opinion tandis que les interactions inter-modèles l'élargissent, et qu'une consigne de persuasion n'augmente pas systématiquement l'influence.
keyPoints: Présente un cadre de débat LLM-LLM contrôlé pour étudier la persuasion et la dynamique des opinions.
Démontre que les interactions entre modèles identiques réduisent l'écart d'opinion, contrairement aux interactions croisées.
Constate qu'une instruction explicite de persuader n'augmente pas de manière fiable l'influence.

items.title: Fig: Automated Multiagent Behavior Elicitor
items.summary: Fig (Finding Interactions in Games) is an agentic system that performs targeted interventions on game environments to elicit complex multiagent behaviors such as cooperation, deception, and sabotage. Tested across six behaviors, Fig's interventions increased attempt rates by an average of 10.9% compared to control games, showing that environments can serve as programmable test beds.
keyPoints: Fig is an agentic system that systematically intervenes in game environments to elicit target behaviors.
Evaluated on six test behaviors including cooperation, deception, betrayal, and sabotage.
Interventions increased target behavior attempt rates by an average of 10.9% over control games.

Testé sur six comportements, Fig a augmenté les taux de tentative de 10,9 % en moyenne par rapport aux témoins.
keyPoints: Fig est un système agentique qui intervient systématiquement dans les jeux pour provoquer des comportements cibles.
Évalué sur six comportements de test incluant la coopération, la tromperie et le sabotage.
Les interventions ont augmenté les taux de tentative de comportement de 10,9 % en moyenne.

items.title: Hidden Messages Between Diffusion Language Model Agents
items.summary: This study investigates whether diffusion language model agents can pass compact hidden messages through continuous denoising states instead of decoded text. Experiments reveal that targeted communication significantly boosts performance on multi-step tasks, demonstrating that the timing of a late information transfer can matter more than recurrent exchanges.
keyPoints: Proposes a method for diffusion language model agents to communicate via continuous denoising states.
Removals and targeted substitutions of hidden messages provide causal evidence of latent communication.
Shows that a single late information transfer can outperform multiple recurrent message exchanges.

en.title: Hidden Messages Between Diffusion Language Model Agents
en.summary: This study investigates whether diffusion language model agents can pass compact hidden messages through continuous denoising states instead of decoded text. Experiments reveal that targeted communication significantly boosts performance on multi-step tasks, demonstrating that the timing of a late information transfer can matter more than recurrent exchanges.
keyPoints: Proposes a method for diffusion language model agents to communicate via continuous denoising states.

fr.title: Messages cachés entre agents de modèles de langage par diffusion
fr.summary: Cette étude examine si des agents de modèles de langage par diffusion peuvent transmettre des messages cachés compacts via des états continus de débruitage plutôt que du texte. Les expériences révèlent qu'une communication ciblée améliore considérablement les performances, démontrant que le timing d'un transfert tardif prime parfois sur des échanges répétés.
keyPoints: Propose une méthode permettant aux agents de communiquer via des états de débruitage continus.
La suppression et la substitution ciblée des messages fournissent des preuves causales de communication latente.
Montre qu'un seul transfert d'information tardif peut surpasser plusieurs échanges récurrents.

items.title: DiffResearch: Accelerating Deep Research with Diffusion Language Models
items.summary: DiffResearch is an open multi-agent deep research framework that replaces autoregressive models with diffusion language models (dLLMs) across all stages. Across 100 benchmark tasks, the diffusion backbone proved roughly 6 times faster end-to-end, and the introduction of dFast provided a 1.99x speedup for decomposition without losing report quality.
keyPoints: Replaces autoregressive backbones with diffusion language models in a deep research framework.
Achieves roughly 6 times faster end-to-end latency across 100 Deep Research Bench tasks.
Introduces dFast to accelerate subquery decomposition by 1.99 times without sacrificing quality.

Sur 100 tâches de référence, le modèle s'est avéré environ 6 fois plus rapide de bout en bout, et le mode dFasT a permis d'accélérer la décomposition sans perte de qualité.
keyPoints: Remplace les modèles autorégressifs par des modèles de langage par diffusion dans la recherche approfondie.
Atteint une latence globale environ 6 fois plus rapide sur 100 tâches du benchmark.
Introduit dFasT pour accélérer la décomposition de requêtes de 1,99 fois sans perte de qualité.

items.title: Simply Logical -- The First Three Decades
items.summary: This paper charts the 30-year evolution of the Prolog textbook Simply Logical from its 1994 print and diskette release to an immersive, fully interactive online edition. Written by the three original authors, the article outlines the pedagogical philosophy, web programming realizations, and authoring toolkits used to shape modern interactive educational materials.
keyPoints: Traces the evolution of the Prolog textbook Simply Logical over three decades.
Combines the perspectives of three authors on pedagogy, web implementation, and authoring tools.
Explores future opportunities for interactive Prolog teaching and educational web technologies.

Rédigé par les trois auteurs, il expose la philosophie pédagogique, les réalisations web et les outils de création pour l'enseignement moderne.
keyPoints: Retrace l'évolution du manuel de Prolog Simply Logical sur trois décennies.
Combine les points de vue de trois auteurs sur la pédagogie, l'implémentation web et les outils.
Explore les opportunités futures pour l'enseignement interactif de Prolog et les technologies web.

items.title: D-Skill: Distilling Teacher Knowledge through Agent Skills
items.summary: D-Skill is a framework that distills black-box teacher capabilities into interpretable natural-language skills by analyzing paired interaction traces without updating model weights. Across multiple benchmarks, D-Skill closes 75%-95% of the teacher-student performance gap, outperforming one-epoch supervised fine-tuning while reducing inference costs by 5.7x to 8.3x.

Across multiple benchmarks, D-Skill closes 75%-95% of the teacher-student performance gap, outperforming one-epoch supervised fine-tuning while reducing inference costs by 5.7x to 8.3x.

fr.title: D-Skill : Distillation des connaissances par compétences d'agent
fr.summary: D-Skill est un cadre qui distille les capacités d'un modèle enseignant en compétences textuelles interprétables en analysant des traces d'interaction, sans modifier les poids du modèle. Sur plusieurs benchmarks, D-Skill comble 75 % à 5 % de l'écart de performance tout en réduisant les coûts d'inférence de 5,7 à 8,3 fois.

items.title: Back Up Before You Regret: Backup Awareness in Coding Agents
items.summary: To address coding agents modifying state without preserving necessary artifacts, the authors introduce RegretBench, a benchmark of 205 tasks based on real-world regret moments. They propose BackUpper, a plugin backup layer that checks tool calls and preserves state prior to modification, achieving high recovery similarity at a minimal cost of $0.014 per task.
keyPoints: Introduces RegretBench to measure backup awareness and regret moments in autonomous coding agents.
Proposes BackUpper, a lightweight plugin layer that automatically backs up modified states.

fr.title: Sauvegarder avant de regretter : la conscience des sauvegardes
fr.summary: Pour contrer le manque de précaution des agents de codage modifiant des environnements sans préserver l'état initial, les auteurs présentent RegretBench, un benchmark de 205 tâches. Ils proposent BackUpper, un module de sauvegarde automatique qui vérifie les appels d'outils et préserve l'état avant modification pour un coût minime de 0,014 $ par tâche.
